#!/bin/bash -l
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --nodes=1
#   --time=1:00:00
#   -A e3sm
#   -p compute
#   --job-name=cice-qc
#   --output=log-cice-qc.o%j
#   --error=log-cice-qc.e%j

#flux: --job-name=cice-qc
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=1h

# Omitted Slurm options: -A e3sm (account) and -p compute (partition)
# Flux accounting/project selection and queue/partition selection are site-specific; no portable equivalents.
# Performance implication: job may be charged differently, have different priority/limits, run on different nodes, or be rejected.

# Omitted Slurm options: --output/--error with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

# Slurm variable $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR is not set under Flux.
cd "${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

source /lcrc/soft/climate/e3sm-unified/load_latest_e3sm_unified_chrysalis.sh

export HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE

export BASE=/lcrc/group/acme/ac.dcomeau/scratch/chrys/20221218.DMPAS-JRA1p5.TL319_EC30to60E2r2.chrysalis.column-package.intel/run
export TEST=/lcrc/group/acme/ac.dcomeau/scratch/chrys/20221218.DMPAS-JRA1p5.TL319_EC30to60E2r2.chrysalis.icepack.intel/run

# Slurm used srun; under Flux, run within the allocation.
flux run -n 1 -c 1 python mpas-seaice.t-test.py "$BASE" "$TEST"

reasons: The original Slurm job specified an account and partition (`-A e3sm`, `-p compute`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/account selection; on sites where these affect eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
